title: Reduce fixed CRT cache setup to one inverse call (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prepare PR4716's fixed CRT cofactor/target cache with **one modular-inverse provider call**, replacing its cited `m+1`-call setup. Claim type: scoped algebraic construction and proof, with exact finite corroboration. No new kappa.

```text
S = product(left moduli), C_j = S/n_j, T = S*s
A = sum(C_j) mod S, v = S*Q mod s
r = inverse((s*A + S*v) mod T, T)       # sole inverse call
alpha_j = s*r mod n_j, mu = S*r mod s
```

The written proof gives the extraction identities and exact coprimality/domain criterion. Current-residue reconstruction and padded invalidity retain the predecessor contract; subsequent evaluations invoke no inverse provider. Only `research/crt-one-inverse-cache/` changes.

## Evidence

- Before: Hiroki KUMAZAKI's #4716 uses `m+1` setup inversions and explicitly makes no inverse-count minimality claim. Its proof and source are pinned as provenance, without replaying predecessor executables.
- After: 209 new cache setups and 8,871 current vectors pass. The `(11,13;17;1)` fixture uses `inverse(1409,2431)=892`, yielding `alpha=(6,6)` and `mu=5`. One-call spies remain active through every evaluation. Sixteen invalid inputs/providers reject; three omission controls detect dropping the target summand or extraction multipliers.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized registered checks pass on CPython 3.12.15 / macOS arm64, timed individually at 0.09 and 0.12 seconds. The registered package runner, committed-byte/source-history preflight, official export integrity and read-only Git-free normal/optimized export replays pass at `16402004d411e15a273d4e6946388d5a93061778`.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/crt-one-inverse-cache/verify.py
```

## Limitations

The new inverse modulus is the full left-and-target product, at most `(m+1)ell` bits when each modulus has at most `ell` bits. The old inverse moduli each have at most `ell` bits. One wider inversion may cost more than the separate calls. All extra division, multiplication and reduction work remains real work; no bit-cost, runtime or minimality claim follows from the provider-call count.

Physical cache preparation/erasure, complete key/caller integration, total tape cost, supplier admission and full multiplication proof remain unrun. No native/Lean/full-selected replay was needed or performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Selected conditional `60403/20000000` remains unchanged.

## Open next questions

- Fix one binary-arithmetic tariff and compare the complete packed setup with the separate inverse calls, including operand widths and every other operation.
- Prepare and erase the packed constants in an actual encoded CRT arena, beginning with `(11,13;17;1)` and a complete ownership/head-return bill.

## Related open work

- #4192 supplies a uniform Beneš compiler/query component and leaves numerical reconstruction/inversion separate; this result changes only fixed cache setup.
- #4187 studies last-K streaming under a supplied evaluator; this module does not close that evaluator or streaming tariff.
- #5092 produces encoded Beneš ROM from supplied rotation descriptors; the packed inverse does not prepare or consume that ROM.
- #5095 composes the actual CRT/Tensor sandwich under inherited numerical/setup premises; this module is not installed into that caller.
- The active [complete CRT repair-control claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4709#discussioncomment-19142272) takes supplied raw/ROM inputs and lowers outer control. Its target is separate from this fixed arithmetic inverse-count construction.
